question.question:
An investor buys 850 shares at USD 41 each. During the holding period one cash dividend of USD 3 per share is paid, and the full dividend cash is reinvested on the ex-dividend date at USD 52 per share. Reinvestment rule: whole shares. Under "fractional" the cash buys an exact fractional share count; under "whole" it buys the largest whole number of shares and the leftover cash is held uninvested at zero interest and counted in ending value. The ending share price is USD 25. Price return is the percent change from USD 41 to USD 25, ignoring dividends. Total return is ending value (all shares held times USD 25, plus any leftover cash) divided by initial cost, minus one, in percent. The dividend contribution is total return minus price return, in percentage points; report it.

Answer format: return only the exact numeric value interpreted in `percent`, using finite-decimal notation when it terminates in base 10 and an irreducible `numerator/denominator` fraction otherwise, with no unit label or additional text.

slots.description: Total number of shares held after reinvestment at the ex-dividend price
Holding-period price return ignoring dividends, in percent
Holding-period total return including reinvested dividend, in percent
